expectations.text: States the intended reader and what they already know, in frontmatter or the opening
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter audience: 'Know Docker and GitHub Actions well; have not used our staging cluster, Vault or the preview setup.'

expectations.text: The first paragraph tells the reader that every PR gets a preview environment and where to find it (the pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev URL)
expectations.evidence: First paragraph: every PR gets a copy at https://pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev about six minutes after each push.

expectations.text: Does not explain Docker basics such as what an image or a container is
expectations.evidence: No definition of image or container.

expectations.text: Explains Vault, or the secret/preview/web path, at first use in words a reader new to it can act on
expectations.evidence: 'Vault, our secrets store, under secret/preview/web' plus how to add a secret.

expectations.text: Explains mailhog, or what happens to emails in a preview, at first use
expectations.evidence: 'MailHog, a mail catcher with a web inbox' at first use.

expectations.text: Omits the story of trying ephemeral databases first, or reduces it to a single sentence of rationale
Writes the concurrent-push failure with the condition (two pushes within about a minute) before the instruction (re-run the job)
expectations.evidence: 'Two pushes within about a minute ... can make the second Helm install fail ... Re-run the failed job.'

expectations.text: States what the reader cannot do: no ssh, and kubectl exec needs staging access most developers lack
expectations.evidence: 'You cannot SSH into a preview ... most developers do not have that access'.

expectations.text: Every heading names its content specifically, and no heading is directly followed by another heading
expectations.evidence: Every heading is a full statement, e.g. 'Preview secrets live in Vault under secret/preview/web'; none stacked.
